Summary

     • The experimental results and detailed predictions support that
    there exists two possible modes of quasi-steady cool flame
    droplet burning behaviour: “Warm” in the NTC regime and “Cold”
    in the low temperature regime.
     • The helium concentration is critical for the observed
    characteristics – promoting the second stage burn or completely
   supressing it.
     • A dynamic coupling between heat generation and heat loss in
    the system.
     • The low temperature kinetics is distinctive and different in the
   second and third stage.
     • Experimental observation with n-dodecane at higher pressure
   and helium exchange validates the “a priori” numerical
    predictions of a three stage behaviour inferred from n-heptane
    simulations.
